name: Overglaze enamelling
summary: Coloured glass enamels are painted on a glazed and fired piece. A third firing at a low heat fixes them on the glaze.
how: Fire the piece with a clear glaze.
Paint the design with enamels of red, green, yellow and blue.
Fire it again in a small muffle kiln at 750 to 850 °C.
Add gold in a last low firing, when the design needs it.

origin.note: Jingdezhen potters add the first on-glaze enamel colours to blue-and-white porcelain.

adoptions.via: Arita potters of the Kakiemon workshop fix a clear red and soft green on a milk-white body.
Kyoto potters paint enamel and gold on a pale crackle glaze, as Ninsei did at the Omuro kiln.
Johann Gregorius Höroldt arrives at Meissen and builds a palette of enamel colours for the hard-paste porcelain.
English porcelain factories paint flowers and insects in enamel on soft-paste tea ware.
Painters of the State Porcelain Factory fix flat planes of black and red enamel on white cups.
